insights.claim: The model-registry Go binary runs on ubi-minimal-pqc, a post-quantum crypto UBI variant, indicating early adoption of PQC-ready infrastructure ahead of broader RHOAI adoption.
insights.reasoning: The runtime base image registry.redhat.io/ubi9/ubi-minimal-pqc is a post-quantum cryptography variant of UBI minimal. This is a forward-looking security choice that prepares the component for PQC migration while maintaining FIPS compliance via system OpenSSL.

insights.claim: Model Registry uses GOEXPERIMENT=strictfipsruntime which is stricter than the older boringcrypto approach, actively failing at runtime if non-FIPS crypto paths are taken rather than silently falling back.
insights.reasoning: strictfipsruntime is the Go 1.24+ replacement for GOEXPERIMENT=boringcrypto. Unlike the older approach which silently substituted BoringCrypto, strictfipsruntime panics if any non-FIPS crypto operation is attempted, providing fail-fast guarantees for FIPS compliance.

insights.claim: The TLS configuration module explicitly validates cipher suites against Go's InsecureCipherSuites() list and rejects any match, providing defense-in-depth beyond build-time FIPS enforcement.
insights.reasoning: This runtime cipher validation complements the build-time FIPS flags by ensuring that even if a cipher suite name is passed via configuration, it will be rejected if Go classifies it as insecure. This is a defense-in-depth pattern not commonly seen in other RHOAI components.

insights.claim: The controller binary (cmd/controller) has no Konflux Dockerfile, meaning its FIPS build posture is not independently verified through the Konflux pipeline.
insights.reasoning: Only two Konflux Dockerfiles exist: Dockerfile.konflux (main Go binary) and jobs/async-upload/Dockerfile.konflux (Python job). The controller is built via cmd/controller/Dockerfile.controller which does not have a Konflux variant, so it may not pass through the same FIPS validation pipeline.
